articles.headline: Ravens send CB Humphrey home, say he'll be inactive after 'criminals' comment
articles.description: The Ravens have sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home from the facility, and he will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was sent home from the team facility and will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers following a recent derogatory comment he made about the city of Baltimore on his podcast, coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday.

Minter said the punishment is for one game only for Humphrey, who will not practice the rest of the week.

The Ravens' discipline comes one day after Humphrey apologized for his remarks.

"He's very remorseful. I think he understands that words mean a lot, especially to people in this city," Minter said before Thursday's practice. "When you say something like that, it's not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate."

On an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" released Wednesday, Humphrey took a swipe at the city when asked what Baltimore was best at making.

After first mentioning "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals."

After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted those remarks.

"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I'm an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments."

Humphrey received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon. The podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page.

Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology in a statement posted to social media, but noted, "a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper.

"I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way."

Scott then added, "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world."

Scott concluded his post by inviting Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."

Humphrey, 30, is in his 10th season with Baltimore and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the Ravens. The No. 16 selection in the 2017 draft by Baltimore, Humphrey has been to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback.

articles.headline: Sources: Broncos sign CB Riley Moss to four-year extension
articles.description: The Broncos locked up a key piece of their secondary by signing cornerback Riley Moss to a four-year extension, sources said.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos once again did some major contract work before Thanksgiving as they have signed cornerback Riley Moss to a four-year extension.

Multiple sources said Thursday the extension, which begins next season and is through the 2030 season, is for $67 million in all. 

Moss, who was the Broncos' third-round pick in the 2023 draft, was scheduled to be one of the team's most prominent unrestricted free agents next March. The signing means the Broncos have their starting cornerbacks -- Pat Surtain II and Moss -- each signed through the 2029 and 2030 seasons, respectively.

The Broncos have two other starters in their secondary who are scheduled to be free agents in March -- safety Brandon Jones and nickel corner Ja'Quan McMillian -- so Moss' deal will give them some flexibility if they want to try to re-sign either Jones or McMillian, or both, in the months ahead.

In November last season, the Broncos signed center Luke Wattenberg, defensive tackle Malcolm Roach and kicker Wil Lutz to contract extensions.

Moss has been a tenacious, high-snap volume player in his time with the Broncos. After several other players have tried, Moss has flourished as the cornerback opposite of Surtain -- a highly active spot.

"Riley just competes, he's got the mentality you need if you're going to be across from Pat,'' Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said. "That's not easy, quarterbacks are going to give you the attention on all of the stress downs, red zone, third down, they don't want Pat, and Riley just plays with physicality, tight coverage and he competes every down.''

Though Joseph has said the Broncos' coverages that are often calculated as man-to-man looks are more combination coverages and not true man-to-man, Moss has still measured out to be one of the league's busiest cornerbacks in recent seasons. Despite leaving the Broncos' Week 9 game against the Carolina Panthers with a concussion followed by the Broncos' Week 10 bye, Moss is still the Broncos' leader in man coverage snaps according to Next Gen stats.

And last season, according to NextGen, Moss led the league in man coverage snaps (333) by a whopping 75 snaps, and Surtain was No. 2 in the league.

Moss, who has had at least 80 tackles in each of the past two seasons and led the NFL with 19 passes defensed in 2025, has 27 tackles in eight games this season. (He missed one with a rib injury.) He has eight passes defensed this season.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic's shot goes cold as Jazz end Lakers' winning streak at 9
articles.description: Luka Doncic said his performance in Wednesday's loss to Utah, in which he shot 10-of-28 and had nine turnovers, was "unacceptable" as the Lakers' win streak ended at nine.
articles.headlineJa: ルカ・ドンチッチのシュートが決まらず、ジャズがレイカーズの9連勝に終止符
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日のユタ戦で、28本中10本しか決められず9回のターンオーバーを記録したルカ・ドンチッチは、自身のパフォーマンスを「受け入れられない」と語った。これによりレイカーズの連勝は9で止まった。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- It was appropriate that the Lakers' thrilling overtime victory Tuesday felt like a party-like atmosphere at Crypto.com Arena, because as with most great parties, L.A. certainly paid for it the next day.

The Lakers' nine-game winning streak was snapped Wednesday in a 109-97 loss to the Jazz, with Utah separating itself down the stretch despite coming in near the bottom of the Western Conference standings.

The outcome lifted Utah to 3-13, good for 14th in the West. L.A. is now 13-3, still atop the conference.

But while the Lakers' late surge to topple the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday showed resiliency while missing two of their starters in Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler, it was hard to tell which team was in first place and which team was the cellar dweller by how Wednesday's fourth quarter played out.

The Jazz outscored the Lakers 31-21, with Luka Doncic committing three of his nine turnovers.

"Honestly," Doncic said afterward, "I just got to do way better than this. This is unacceptable for my part. I got to lead the team in better ways."

It wasn't just that he personally coughed up the ball as many times as all of his teammates did combined. It was that when he shot it, he didn't connect nearly as often as he has been accustomed to in a start to the season that has already generated MVP buzz for the 27-year-old guard.

In Doncic's first 12 games, he averaged 39 points on 48.6% shooting, 40.6% from 3, 7.8 assists, 7.2 rebounds and 1.9 steals.

In his past two games in the back-to-back against Charlotte and Utah without Reaves, who is recovering from a bruised left heel, he averaged 32.5 points on 37.1% shooting, 25% from 3, 7.0 assists, 6.0 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 7.0 turnovers.

"I mean, the shot creation that is required from him, I think it takes its toll," Lakers coach JJ Redick said when asked about Doncic's energy level as L.A. played its third game in the past four days without Reaves. "That's the luxury of having two really elite creators, and obviously when they're both in the lineup, it makes things a little bit easier."

Doncic did not accept his coach's forgiveness for tired legs catching up to a star player shouldering the load during a packed stretch of the schedule.

"That can't be an excuse," Doncic said. "All NBA teams play 82 games, so that can't be an excuse."

Redick said before the game that Reaves progressed to an on-court workout for the first time since sustaining the foot injury last week in Milwaukee. His status for Friday's game against the Sacramento Kings is still to be determined.

Kessler's return Wednesday from a one-game absence because of soreness in his right leg didn't have much of an impact.

"It was a tough night for me," said Kessler, who finished with 10 points and 11 rebounds against his former team, but shot 3-for-7 from the field and 4-for-10 from the foul line. articles.headline: Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft named Hall of Fame finalists for 2nd straight year
articles.description: Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft have both advanced to the final round of voting for the Pro Football Hall of Fame for the second straight year.
articles.body:
Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft, key to the New England Patriots' dynasty of six Super Bowl titles, will be considered side by side once again for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Belichick and Kraft have both advanced to the final round of voting for the second straight year, the Hall of Fame announced Thursday. Belichick, currently the coach at North Carolina, and Kraft, the Patriots owner, advanced from the coach and contributor subcommittees, respectively, earlier this week to be considered for the Class of 2027.

They will join 13 players, from all eras, to be chosen in the coming weeks by the Hall's Board of Selectors. Those 15 candidates, all considered and voted on together, will be trimmed to the Hall's Class of 2027 in the weeks before the Super Bowl. A class can now have between three and seven inductees, with the most likely class size to be four or five each year. It takes an 80% vote from the selectors in the final voting for enshrinement.

Neither Belichick nor Kraft was selected for the Hall's four-member Class of 2026, resulting in a firestorm of criticism about the selection procedures and committee makeup.

Belichick, the second-winningest coach in NFL history (333 wins, regular season and playoffs combined) behind Hall of Famer Don Shula, won six Super Bowls with the Patriots as a head coach and two more as a New York Giants assistant coach. His omission last year, in his first appearance on the ballot, was a key topic around Super Bowl week in February.

Kraft advanced from the contributor subcommittee last year for the first time. The Patriots' owner since 1994, Kraft hired Belichick in 2000 and the team went on to win six Super Bowls and play in nine Super Bowls overall in their time together. With Kraft as owner, the Patriots have won 20 AFC East titles and played in 11 Super Bowls, including last season when the Patriots advanced to Super Bowl LX.

In September, after a 2½-year review of the selection process that began before Belichick and Kraft's 2026 snub, the Hall announced a smaller group of selectors -- 28, down from 50, with no regional designations -- and the removal of the seniors category for players. The subcommittees for the coach and contributor categories remained in place.

Each year, 25 of the 28 selectors, with three alternates, will vote for the induction class. The alternates will be determined on an annual basis.

The selectors will narrow the final list of candidates from 15 to 10 to seven. Selectors then may vote for six of the seven. Any candidate receiving 80% approval would be inducted.

The Class of 2027 will be announced during the NFL Honors show in Los Angeles during Super Bowl week. The induction ceremony will be held in August in Canton, Ohio.

articles.headline: Whether it's against backup QBs or not, the Bills' defense is rolling
articles.description: Buffalo will face another backup QB in Week 11 with Kyle McCord set to start in place of Malik Willis for the Dolphins.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills are executing something about as close to a midseason worst-to-first transformation as you'll ever see, albeit with a massive caveat.

Less than one month ago, the Bills trudged through their bye week with the NFL's 30th-ranked scoring defense and 31st-ranked total defense. So naturally in the weeks since, the Bills have allowed the fewest points and second fewest yards among the teams that have played three games.

It's been a steep turnaround for a Bills defense that's gone from the unit holding back the highest-scoring offense to a strength in its own right. But that turnaround has also coincided with the Bills playing almost exclusively against backup quarterbacks, a trend that'll continue when the Bills (8-1) host the Miami Dolphins (1-8) at Highmark Stadium on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

So, as obvious as the answer might seem, it's worth asking the question: Is the game really that different when you're facing an NFL backup quarterback rather than a starter?

"It's definitely not the starters," Bills safety Amani Hooker told ESPN. "Nothing's easy. But it's just like anything else. The better talented guy is off the field in any position, it's not good for their team. I'm sure they feel the same way."

"I don't get to choose who I play. I just play," defensive lineman Ed Oliver adds. "Hell, who cares? If I got to choose who I could play, s---. I guess it would be a starter. But you don't get to choose. That's kind of how football works. People get hurt. Next man up."

Ask Bills players and coaches alike and they'll say there's real belief the defense is executing better regardless of the opposing quarterbacks. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard points to how the defense is steadily getting better at holding strong on second- and third-and-long.

Communication has improved in the secondary. Turnovers are up. Sacks are up. Third-down conversion rates are down. The defense is playing better in just about every way.

But again, it's tough to separate those improvements from the circumstances. Before the bye, the Bills played games against the likes of C.J. Stroud, Jared Goff, Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford.

Since, it's been games against rookie Joe Fagnano (after Lamar Jackson was injured on the Ravens' first offensive play and backup Tyler Huntley went out early in the second quarter) and Carson Wentz -- two quarterbacks who've since been replaced by trade acquisitions. Then it was rookie Cade Klubnik (for about half of the game with Geno Smith going out) making his NFL debut, with Kyle McCord, who also made his debut last week, up next.

"Just like anything in this profession, you can make a reason or an excuse and try to point to, well, we're only having success because of this," Bills coach Joe Brady says. "Our job is to go out there and play to our capabilities and to our standard, regardless of who's on the other side of the football.

articles.headline: Arda Güler signs new six-year Real Madrid contract
articles.description: Arda Güler has signed a new, long-term contract at Real Madrid until 2032, the club said on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Arda Güler has signed a new, long-term contract at Real Madrid until 2032, the club said on Wednesday.

Midfielder Güler, 21, has been one of Madrid's outstanding players this season, starring under new coach José Mourinho.

Güler joined Madrid as a teenager in July 2023, and is already an established international with Türkiye.

"Real Madrid C. F. and Arda Güler have agreed to an extension of the player's contract, keeping him with the club until June 30, 2032," the club said on Wednesday.

"Over his four seasons wearing our jersey, he has made 126 appearances and won five trophies: one Champions League, one FIFA Club World Cup, one UEFA Super Cup, one LaLiga title, and one Spanish Supercopa.

"He is a Turkish international, having earned 38 caps for his national team to date.

"Last September, he received the Breakthrough Player of the Season award for the 2025-2026 Champions League."

Güler has made 12 appearances in LaLiga this season -- contributing three goals and four assists -- with Madrid currently second in the table, three points behind Barcelona.

He scored a sensational free kick against Belgium to give his side the lead.

What you need to know for Thursday

On Thursday, Towns visits his former team, the Minnesota Timberwolves, who remain without Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo. It's one of four games on the slate.

Victor Wembanyama finished with 25 points and 18 rebounds against the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, but the San Antonio Spurs had their 12-game winning streak snapped. San Antonio hosts the LA Clippers and will be without Dylan Harper and Tobias Harris.

The Memphis Grizzlies have won four straight, and Cam Spencer is coming off a 26-point, seven-assist performance against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday. Let's take a closer look at Thursday's matchups, along with some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino: Man United players must relearn 'about being winners'
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino has said his first job as Manchester United's new head coach is to remind the players how to win after a miserable start to the season.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has said his first job as Manchester United's new head coach is to remind the players how to win after a miserable start to the season.

Pochettino began work at Carrington on Wednesday after taking over from Michael Carrick. He's inherited a team 18th in the table with just one Premier League win all season.

The 54-year-old will take charge for the first time against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday and ahead of the game, he said his players must quickly rediscover the feeling of winning matches.

"The most important thing is for us to start to work hard to recover those feelings about being winners, to win games, to perform," Pochettino said in his first full interview since his appointment.

"But that is not only to talk about winning, it is about starting to act and to change things and to try to affect in a good way all the areas to try to really believe that we can recover that feeling to win."

A run of eight league games without a win has seen United slip into the Premier League's bottom three. Their worst start to a season for 40 years has raised the possibility of relegation to the second tier.

But Pochettino insists he doesn't want his squad playing with that pressure on their shoulders and instead told the players to "express their talent."

"I think it is a mistake to see the situation," he said.

"We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, circumstances are circumstances and we need to be responsible of the circumstances.

- Manchester United finally get Mauricio Pochettino after a decade of near misses

- Predicting how all 20 Premier League teams will finish the season

- Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Man United: 'You will see, give me time'

"The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now, is to work with them and try to take the pressure.

"Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back."

Pochettino: Sir Alex Ferguson 'the best' in history

Pochettino has been close to joining United in the past and was interviewed for the job in 2024 shortly after leaving Chelsea.

Finally in the hot seat after signing a contract until 2029, he revealed his affinity for the club began more than 25 years ago when he attended the 1999 Champions League final victory over Bayern Munich in Barcelona, while he was a player for Espanyol.

"That was an iconic final," he said.

"From there I was so excited to see Manchester United and more with the admiration for Sir Alex Ferguson. For me, the best coach in the history of the sport. Now being the head coach is an honour and a privilege. The excitement to be here is massive."

articles.headline: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch
articles.description: "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released Thursday following a 13-year wait since GTA V.
articles.body:
Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale.

That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013.

More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release.

"So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said.

Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013. 

Seattle and Denver were starting their Super Bowl runs

The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver.

The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns.

Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released.

Miami Heat looking to three-peat

The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles.

Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship.

The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme.

Five stars preparing to go one-and-done

The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters.

In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects.

Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden.

articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ全20チームのシーズン最終順位を予想
articles.descriptionJa: 10試合を終え、2026-27シーズンのプレミアリーグ全チームの最終順位を予想するための十分なデータが集まった。
articles.body:
At a glance, the Premier League table doesn't look that weird. The defending champs are in first, and Manchester City, Liverpool, and Chelsea all sit within the top five.

Except ... then there's Brighton in second place -- and not just that, but Brighton with a plus-19 goal differential. Or, put another way: Brighton with a goal differential that's better than Arsenal and Manchester City have combined to produce so far.

Oh, and then there's Everton -- who lost Iliman Ndiaye this summer and failed to sign a striker -- tied with Chelsea on points. Below them, there's Bournemouth, who lost their theoretically transformative manager, Andoni Iraola, to Liverpool. And below them, there's Brentford, who have a better goal differential than everyone in the league other than Brighton, Arsenal, and Man City.

Go further down the standings and Tottenham are in 11th, which is weird but what exact kind of weirdness is completely in the eye of the beholder. Two spots down from there, we've got Hull City, who were supposed to be one of the worst Premier League teams we've ever seen and who, through 10 games, have scored just as many goals as they've conceded.

None of the other promoted sides are in the bottom three, either. Instead, we've got a Europa League team in Crystal Palace anchoring the bottom, a Conference League team in Sunderland one spot ahead of them, and a Champions League team in Manchester United that is now managed by the guy who managed the U.S. men's national team this past summer.

And that's just the surface level. There's even more weirdness once you go a little deeper, like the fact that, say Nottingham Forest have attempted more shots than Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City, and Chelsea while also conceding the fewest shots of any team in the league. Or that, I don't know, Fulham have generated more touches in the opposition penalty area than anyone other than Man City or Arsenal?

With the financial rise of the Premier League's non-Big Six and the leaguewide trend toward man-marking and aggressive pressing, the things that have won soccer games in the past are not necessarily winning soccer games right now. And that makes it a little harder to predict what will win soccer games for the rest of the season.

However, we're 10 games into the current campaign -- a nice stopping point at which to ask ourselves: What will the Premier League table look like once we get to May?

How to predict the rest of the Premier League season

In the past, one of the easiest ways to predict the rest of the season was to just look at the Premier League table sorted by expected goals.

Obviously, it wouldn't tell you everything. But once you got to the 10-game mark, the best teams tended to be the teams that were creating more and better chances than their opponents.

articles.headline: Historic usage rates are fueling Luka Doncic and the Lakers' offense
articles.description: Doncic is pushing the boundaries of basketball production. But could that actually hurt the Lakers' title hopes?
articles.body:
Is there such a thing as too much Luka magic?

That question might seem blasphemous to Los Angeles Lakers fans savoring Luka Doncic's scorching start for the NBA's third-ranked offense, but it's one worth monitoring as he pushes the boundaries of basketball production.

Doncic has jumped to the front of the NBA MVP conversation by averaging 38.1 points per game, which would eclipse Michael Jordan for the highest scoring average since the 1976 NBA/ABA merger. But the Lakers guard is also posting a historic usage rate -- the percentage of his team's possessions he ends with a shot attempt, free throw attempt or turnover -- that sidles him with one of the heaviest offensive burdens in league history.

Given that ultra-high usage stars have always fallen short of winning a championship, should Doncic's heavy load start to raise alarm bells?

Los Angeles is tied for the league's best record at 13-3, largely because none of its opponents have effectively slowed down Doncic, who already has seven 40-point and two 50-point performances. The Lakers have a juicy plus-15.3 net rating when the Slovenian star is on the court and have racked up seven double-digit victories.

L.A.'s extraordinary reliance on Doncic rekindles a debate about the perils of ball dominance. When one player is so responsible for his team's success, it leaves the roster exposed if he sustains an injury and increases the possibility the player might succumb to diminishing returns.

This is well-worn narrative territory that dates back decades: Jordan needs to pass more. Allen Iverson can't do it by himself. Russell Westbrook is a ball hog.

Now, the Lakers' title aspirations will hinge on whether they can avoid some of the pitfalls that tripped up previous high-usage superstars.

Why Doncic faces a daunting precedent

The conditions are just right for Doncic to break calculators with his scoring and usage: The Lakers lost five of their top seven scorers from last season and don't ask any starting forwards to be major offensive contributors. At 27, he is in his prime, has worked his way into excellent shape and is seemingly on a mission to make the most of his new status as the face of the post-LeBron James Lakers.

"[Doncic excels because of] the volume of the three-point shot combined with his ability to get to the free throw line," Lakers coach JJ Redick said Wednesday. "If you look at most elite scorers, it's a tale as old as time. Jordan, Kobe [Bryant], they got to the free throw line. It's that, and when you're shooting 12 or 13 shots a game at 40 percent from three, you can really score at volume."

As a result, Doncic's early work has been off the charts.

This graphic shows the scoring and usage rate for the 285 players who have logged the most minutes during the 2026-27 season. Doncic sits all alone in the upper right corner with a significant gap between himself and a tier of A-list stars that includes Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Victor Wembanyama, Stephen Curry and Giannis Ante

articles.headline: Valentín Barco on Chelsea career so far: 'I think I can give a lot more'
articles.description: Chelsea's Valentín Barco has said he is confident that he's still a long way away from reaching his full potential.
articles.body:
Chelsea's Valentín Barco has said he is confident that he's still a long way away from reaching his full potential.

The Argentina international returned to Chelsea this week having not featured in his country's two international friendlies, a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay and a 7-0 rout of Costa Rica.

"As a player, you always want to play so you are not happy when you don't but I understand this is the best national team in the world," Barco told ESPN. "But I'm happy to come to the national team, to continue to represent my country. I will now try to play at Chelsea and contribute."

Barco, 22, was part of Argentina's squad that finished runners-up to Spain at the 2026 World Cup.

He signed a contract with Chelsea through 2033 following his strong performances for Strasbourg, the club he joined from Brighton & Hove Albion in January 2025.

Returning to the Premier League was a priority for Barco, who made only seven appearances during his time at Brighton. Barco has had limited playing time under Xabi Alonso but said he believes he will eventually shine at Stamford Bridge.

"I think I can give a lot more," he said. "I also said the same thing when I was at Strasbourg; even when I was playing well, I knew I could give more because I know what I can give.

"I have a lot of confidence in myself so I have to keep working to continue growing."

Barco has one goal in even appearances, four of which in the Premier League.

- O'Hanlon: Predicting how all 20 Premier League teams will finish the season

articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、10年にわたる後追いを経てついにマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノを招聘
articles.descriptionJa: 長年にわたる惜しい機会やチャンスを逃した末、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは10年越しの追求を経て、ついにマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノを監督に迎える。
articles.body:
It feels a bit like destiny for Mauricio Pochettino to end up at Manchester United. After all, their flirtation with the former Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and U.S. men's national team manager began more than 10 years ago.

In May 2016, amid mounting doubts over Louis van Gaal's future, Sir Alex Ferguson asked to meet Pochettino at a London restaurant. Jose Mourinho was already being lined up to replace Van Gaal, but Ferguson still asked the League Managers Association secretary for Pochettino's number.

The two-hour lunch at Scott's Restaurant in Mayfair would have stayed private, except the pair -- and Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez -- were caught by paparazzi on the street outside.

Concerned about the speculation, Tottenham insisted it was just a "social occasion between colleagues." To quiet the noise further, they moved up an announcement that Pochettino had verbally agreed to a new five-year contract. Mourinho was confirmed as Van Gaal's successor weeks later.

United have made five permanent appointments since Pochettino's meeting with Ferguson and the former Argentina defender has never been far away.

When Mourinho was sacked in December 2018, Pochettino -- impressing at Spurs -- was considered the top choice for many Old Trafford executives. But with Pochettino under contract at Tottenham, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was given the caretaker role to steady the ship. Solskjaer won his first five games and in January 2019, United traveled to Spurs and won 1-0 to make it six from six.

Sources at United said there was no "defining moment" that decided Solskjaer would get the job permanently, but victory over Pochettino's Spurs was viewed as "a very positive sign." Two months later, Solskjaer signed a three-year deal; Pochettino was sacked by Tottenham in November 2019, five months after reaching the UEFA Champions League final.

Out of work and available, his name hung over Solskjaer's reign every time there was a blip. It reached the point in January 2021 that United bosses admitted they were "relieved" when Pochettino took over at Paris Saint-Germain. The feeling at the time was that the speculation had become a distraction and that Solskjaer would get more breathing space with Pochettino out of the picture as a potential replacement.

Solskjaer lasted another 11 months. When the Norwegian was sacked in November 2021, United opted for another caretaker in Ralf Rangnick and Pochettino was earmarked early on as a potential permanent appointment at the end of the season. It never materialized.

Form under Rangnick at the end of the 2021-22 season was so bad that United wanted to lift the mood and announce a permanent successor before the end of the campaign. In the end, it was a close call between Pochettino and Erik ten Hag. Crucially, Ajax allowed Ten Hag to negotiate with United during the season.
